To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
butyl paraben causes oxidative stress and neuroinflammation in the rat brain.
butyl paraben causes oxidative stress and neuroinflammation in the brain, and these effects resemble the brain pathology in autism.
paraben intoxication induces oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction in the rat brain, and the autistic rat model exhibits the same markers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between oxidative stress, inflammation, energy metabolism and mitochondrial dysfunction in the rat brain following butyl paraben exposure.
a better understanding of the role of oxidative stress, inflammation, and mitochondrial dysfunctions in paraben intoxication.
the potential role of butyl paraben in the pathogenesis of ASDs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
butyl parabene intoxication may be a contributing factor to autism.
butyl paraben may be one of the factors contributing to the pathophysiology of autism.
paraben intoxication may be a contributing cause to the brain pathology observed and/or may contribute to the pathogenesis in the diagnosed ASD rat model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain oxidative stress markers are increased and the brain energy metabolism is disturbed.
butyl paraben may, at least in part, either cause or exacerbate the neurotoxicity and oxidative stress in ASDs.
paraben intoxication in the brain is a potential factor in the development of ASDs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of butyl paraben in food, cosmetics and drugs is not safe and should be avoided.
the brain oxidative stress and inflammatory biomarkers in the paraben treated rats were similar to the brain biomarkers in the autistic like rat model.
paraben may contribute to the pathophysiology of the autistic brain.
